title: Diffraction
target: Explain spreading around edges and through openings.
criteria: Use a wave picture to justify spreading.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: Waves of wavelength 0.8 m encounter openings 0.8 m and 8 m wide. Which gives more pronounced spreading relative to opening width?
options: The 8 m opening.
The 0.8 m opening.
Both always produce no spreading.
Only opening color matters.
cpa.guide: Diffraction is pronounced when opening size is comparable to wavelength.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: An opening is fixed. Wavelength increases from 2 cm to 6 cm. What general trend is expected?
options: The waves must stop carrying energy.
More noticeable diffraction.
Less noticeable diffraction in every geometry.
No possible change.
cpa.guide: Larger wavelength relative to the opening generally produces greater angular spreading.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A wave spreads after passing through a narrow gap without entering a new medium. What effect is this?
options: Doppler shift caused by a moving source.
Refraction caused by a new propagation speed.
Diffraction.
A change in electric charge.
cpa.guide: Gap-induced spreading is diffraction, even without a medium change.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A ray changes direction at a stationary water-depth boundary because its speed changes. Which name best fits?
options: Complete destructive interference.
Diffraction solely because any direction changed.
Reflection necessarily back to its source.
Refraction.
cpa.guide: Refraction is associated with propagation-speed change at a boundary.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: Which wavefront description best represents strong diffraction through a small opening?
options: Curved fronts spread outward from the opening.
The fronts become solid moving material.
The fronts terminate because energy cannot pass.
All fronts remain narrow straight segments forever.
cpa.guide: A small aperture can act like a spreading wave source; curved fronts indicate multiple propagation directions.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Low-frequency sound is heard around a doorway more readily than very high-frequency sound in a simple diffraction comparison. What explains the trend?
options: Its longer wavelength is larger relative to the doorway.
All high-frequency sound is destroyed at corners.
Low-frequency sound has no need for a medium.
Its wave speed must be much higher in the same air.
cpa.guide: At similar sound speed, lower f means longer λ and generally more diffraction around the opening.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.
